content_preview.title: PHP 8.6 Beta 3 Adds a Native clamp() Function and SortDirection Enum Ahead of November GA
content_preview.summary: PHP 8.6.0 Beta 3 landed with a native clamp() function, a SortDirection enum, and a trim() whitespace fix, as the release heads toward a November 19 GA.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The PHP project released [PHP 8.6.0 Beta 3](https://www.php.net/index.php) on September 10, 2026, the third beta of the upcoming 8.6 series and the last scheduled beta before the release candidate phase begins. The [PHP.net homepage](https://www.php.net/index.php) describes it as the "Third beta release of PHP 8.6.0" and notes the next milestone, RC1, is "planned for 24 September 2026."

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News article on PHP 8.6.0 Beta 3, covering four RFC-backed language changes (clamp(), SortDirection enum, trim() form-feed handling, grapheme_strrev()) plus the release timeline. Clear sections (Overview, What We Know, Release Timeline, What We Don't Know). Word count of 611 is appropriate for the News category (400-1200).
editor_notes.source_verification: All 7 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallbacks, no suspicious_patterns). Sha256 of every decompressed snapshot matches the manifest exactly (integrity verified via gunzip + sha256sum). Read all 7 snapshots in full: source-0.html.gz (php.net homepage) — confirms '10 Sep 2026 PHP 8.6.0 Beta 3 is available for testing', 'the third beta release of PHP 8.6.0, Beta 3', and 'The next release will be RC 1, planned for 24 September 2026' verbatim. source-1.html.gz (pre-release-builds.php) — confirms both quoted sentences verbatim: 'The downloads on this page are not meant to be run in production. They are for testing only.' and 'These builds are meant for the community to test whether no inadvertent changes have been made, and whether no regressions have been introduced.' Also confirms the 8.6.0beta3 source tarball date of 10 Sep 2026. source-2.html.gz (wiki.php.net/todo/php86) — confirms the full timeline table verbatim: Beta 3 Sep 10 2026, hard feature freeze Sep 22 2026 quoted exactly ('features, whether requiring an RFC or not, must be merged only with approval from the RMs'), RC1 Sep 24, RC2 Oct 8, RC3 Oct 22, RC4 Nov 5 (confirming the 'two-week cadence' paraphrase), GA Nov 19 2026, and the Aug 13 2026 Beta 1/soft-feature-freeze entry supporting the 'concluded at the soft feature freeze in August' claim. source-3.html.gz (rfc/clamp_v2) — confirms the clamp(mixed $value, mixed $min, mixed $max): mixed signature, the ValueError conditions (min>max, NAN), the worked example 'clamp(6, min: 1, max: 3) // 3', the 'Final result: 23 3 6' vote tally, and the parameter-order sentence naming 'C++, C#, Python, Java'. Does NOT contain the phrase 'performance benefit(s)' anywhere in the page — see concerns. source-4.html.gz (rfc/sort_direction_enum) — confirms the enum code block verbatim, the orderBy() example verbatim, both quoted sentences verbatim ('PHP's standard library has no type-safe way to express sort direction.' and 'every major PHP framework and library ends up defining its own sort direction type.'), and 'Final result: 22 2 2'. source-5.html.gz (rfc/trim_form_feed) — confirms the ASCII 12 / \f default-whitespace-mask claim, the quoted sentence 'Most modern programming languages treat \f as whitespace in their trimming functions.' verbatim, the before/after var_dump example, the Python/JavaScript/Rust/Go comparison list, and 'Final result: 25 0 0'. Does not mention chop() anywhere — see concerns (chop() is a native PHP alias of rtrim(), so the claim is true, but it is not supported by this or any of the 7 cited sources). source-6.html.gz (rfc/grapheme_strrev) — confirms the grapheme_strrev() proposal, the emoji-modifier and RTL Arabic code examples, and 'Final result: 20 0 0'.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All four RFC vote tallies, all dates in the release timeline, and five of six direct quotes are verified verbatim against the snapshots. One quote is not verbatim: the clamp() paragraph states the RFC 'argues a native implementation offers "performance benefits"' — the string 'benefit' does not appear anywhere in the clamp_v2 RFC snapshot. The RFC's actual performance language is 'a native function would be even slightly faster than userland implementation using ternary' — a real but differently-worded claim. This is a paraphrase dressed as a direct quote, not a fabricated fact (the underlying claim — that native clamp() is faster — is accurate and sourced), so it is recoverable via a corrections note rather than a headline/lead-breaking error. Separately, the body's parenthetical that the form-feed whitespace change also affects chop() is accurate (chop() is a documented native alias of rtrim() in PHP) but is not stated in any of the 7 cited sources — a minor unsourced elaboration on a true fact, not a misstatement.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Attribution to 'the RFC' and named RFC authors' arguments is handled with appropriate hedging language ('the RFC argues').
editor_notes.originality: No existing Machine Herald coverage of PHP 8.6 Beta 3 or these four specific RFCs. grep across src/content/articles/2026-08 and 2026-09 for 'PHP 8.6' returns no hits. Genuinely new topic. The internal cross-reference to the BSD 3-Clause licensing article (/article/2026-05/26-php-retires-its-23-year-old-custom-license-and-adopts-bsd-3-clause-starting-with-php-86) was checked and resolves: the file exists at src/content/articles/2026-05/26-php-retires-its-23-year-old-custom-license-and-adopts-bsd-3-clause-starting-with-php-86.md with exactly that slug, so the link target is valid and the underlying claim (BSD 3-Clause adoption starting with PHP 8.6) was independently fact-checked and approved in that prior review.
concerns: Paraphrase presented as a direct quote: the article states the clamp() RFC 'argues a native implementation offers "performance benefits"'. This exact phrase does not appear in the RFC (rfc/clamp_v2) snapshot — the word 'benefit' does not occur anywhere in the page. The RFC's actual wording is that a native function 'would be even slightly faster than userland implementation using ternary, while providing some extra validation out of the box: NAN handling and verifying min <= max'. The substance is accurate; only the quote-marked phrasing is not verbatim. Recoverable via a corrections note.

Minor unsourced elaboration: the article states the form-feed default-whitespace change applies to trim(), ltrim(), rtrim(), and chop(). The cited RFC (rfc/trim_form_feed) names only trim(), ltrim(), and rtrim() — chop() never appears in the snapshot. The claim is true (chop() is PHP's built-in alias of rtrim()) but is not supported by any of the 7 cited sources. Noting for the record; not significant enough on its own to warrant a separate corrections entry given the underlying fact is correct and not central to the article's claims.
recommendations: Add php.net and wiki.php.net to config/source_allowlist.txt — these are the official primary sources for PHP language RFCs and releases, and this is the second article (after the May 2026 BSD-3-Clause licensing piece) to cite them without a matching allowlist entry.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News article. Four RFC vote tallies, the full release timeline, and five of six direct quotes are verified verbatim across all 7 read-and-hash-verified source snapshots. One clause in the clamp() section ('performance benefits') is a paraphrase presented in quote marks rather than the RFC's actual wording — a single recoverable issue, not a pattern, and not in the headline/summary/lead (which are fully supported: Beta 3 release, clamp(), SortDirection enum, trim() fix, November GA target are all confirmed by the php.net/wiki.php.net snapshots). The internal cross-reference to the prior BSD 3-Clause licensing article resolves correctly. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS, with a corrections note documenting the misquoted phrase.
